title: What RSA training do staff and licensees need in Victoria?
description: Victorian RSA rules: which licenses need it, the one month deadline for new staff, the 3 year refresher, certificates kept on site and fines under the Act.
shortAnswer: In Victoria, staff who offer, take orders or payment for, pour or serve alcohol at a venue with a general, on-premises, late night or packaged liquor license need a current RSA Certificate of Completion from a Liquor Control Victoria approved course, obtained before or within one month of first supplying alcohol. The certificate lasts three years, renewed through a free online refresher, and the licensee must keep copies on site for inspectors.
keyTakeaways: Staff at general, on-premises, late night and packaged liquor venues need a current RSA Certificate of Completion if their job involves offering, taking orders or payment for, pouring or serving alcohol.
New staff must complete RSA training before they start supplying alcohol or within one month of the date they first supply it.
Certificates are current for three years; the free RSA Refresher takes about 90 minutes online and now includes a sexual harassment and assault module.
Licensees must keep a copy of each staff member's current certificate at the venue and produce it immediately if a liquor inspector or Victoria Police asks.
Under sections 108AA to 108AE of the Liquor Control Reform Act 1998, training failures carry a maximum penalty of $12,546 and certificate keeping failures $1,046.
regulator: Liquor Control Victoria (LCV), with liquor inspectors and Victoria Police enforcing
appliesTo: Staff who supply alcohol at venues with a general, on-premises, late night or packaged liquor license
Licensees of those license types, and the responsible person in charge for company, association, co-operative, TAFE, university and council licensees
Applicants for a permanent license or license transfer (other than a BYO permit or pre-retail license)
Late night licensees and licensees who record a demerit point (Advanced RSA)

sections.heading: Who must hold an RSA certificate in Victoria?

blocks.text: Anyone who supplies alcohol at a Victorian venue with a general, on-premises, late night or packaged liquor license needs a current RSA Certificate of Completion. [Liquor Control Victoria](https://www.vic.gov.au/rsa-training) defines supplying broadly: the requirement applies if the job includes offering alcoholic drinks, taking orders or payment for alcohol, or pouring or serving alcoholic drinks.

That definition captures more roles than bar staff. A checkout operator in a bottle shop who takes payment for alcohol, a floor attendant who takes drink orders, and a host who offers wine at a table all fall within it. Other license types, such as restaurant and cafe or limited licenses, are not on the list unless a special condition on the license requires RSA.

A person under 18 can complete RSA training but must wait until they are 18 to serve alcohol. Applicants for a permanent license or a license transfer also need RSA, except for a BYO permit or pre-retail license.

sections.heading: How soon must new staff complete RSA training?

blocks.text: New staff must complete RSA training either before they start supplying alcohol or within one month of the date they first supply it. The one month window is a grace period for onboarding, not an exemption: a staff member still inside it can serve, but the licensee carries the risk if the deadline passes without a certificate.

The legal duty sits with the licensee. Section 108AB of the Liquor Control Reform Act 1998 makes it an offense for a licensee to fail to ensure that anyone who sells, offers for sale or serves liquor has completed an approved RSA program, and section 108AC covers staff whose last program is more than three years old, according to the [Liquor Control Victoria offenses table](https://www.vic.gov.au/liquor-offences-and-fines).

sections.heading: What does the Victorian RSA course include?

blocks.text: The approved Victorian course includes the national unit Provide responsible service of alcohol (SITHFAB021) plus Victorian topics: state liquor laws, drink spiking, ID checks and preventing secondary supply, use of prone restraint, harm minimization strategies, and compliance and enforcement.

RSA training, including the refresher, now includes a module called Sexual Harassment and Assault: Recognise, Prevent and Respond. After a provider reports completion, Liquor Control Victoria emails a certificate number, the learner completes a pre training survey, the module and a post training survey on the Liquor Control Victoria Learning Hub, and only then downloads the RSA Certificate of Completion. A learner who finishes the provider course but skips the Learning Hub step does not yet have the certificate an employer must keep.

blocks.title: Practical point
blocks.text: The provider's Statement of Attainment is not the document Liquor Control Victoria asks employers to keep. Employers need the RSA Certificate of Completion downloaded from the Learning Hub.

sections.heading: How often must RSA be refreshed in Victoria?

blocks.text: Every three years. Staff must complete the RSA Refresher course every 3 years to keep the certificate current, and a certificate more than 3 years old is not valid for work. The refresher is free, takes about 90 minutes, and is completed online with the original certificate number.

Licensees of general, on-premises, late night and packaged liquor licenses must also complete the refresher every three years. Where the licensee is a company, incorporated association, co-operative, TAFE, university or municipal council, the [licensee obligations page](https://www.vic.gov.au/licensee-training-obligations) says the responsible person in charge must do the refresher every three years.

Three years is shorter than the five year cycle used in New South Wales, so national operators should not apply one refresh rule across states. See [NSW RSA competency card rules](/regulations/responsible-service-of-alcohol-training-nsw) for the comparison and [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles) for scheduling methods.

sections.heading: When is Advanced RSA training required?

blocks.text: Licensees and the responsible person in charge of a late night (general) or late night (on-premises) license must complete Advanced RSA training within 6 months of the license being granted or of a demerit point being recorded. General and on-premises licensees must also complete it within 6 months of a demerit point being recorded.

New license applicants, other than for a pre-retail license or BYO permit, must complete new entrant training and RSA training, and the regulator cannot decide the application until training is complete. Licensees can apply for an extension of time, or in rare situations a permanent exemption, from RSA training requirements, but not from Advanced RSA.

sections.heading: What records must a Victorian licensee keep, and what are the fines?

blocks.text: The licensee must keep a copy of each required staff member's current RSA Certificate of Completion at the venue, as a photocopy or digital copy, and make it immediately available if liquor inspectors or Victoria Police ask. Liquor Control Victoria publishes optional RSA and Advanced RSA register templates to track completion and refresh dates.

For audit preparation more broadly, see [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) and the glossary entry on the [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records the RSA certificate as an external credential with a three year validity rule and links it to venue level procedures, such as ID checking and drink spiking response, that are assessed internally. Operators running venues in more than one state can hold each state's refresh rule against the same role. See [compliance programs](/programs/compliance).

faqs.q: Does an interstate RSA certificate work in Victoria?
faqs.a: Not automatically. A person trained interstate can apply for the free bridging course, called RSA Refresher, which issues a Victorian certificate, if the original training was approved by a state or territory liquor authority and completed within the last 3 years. Liquor Control Victoria allows 10 working days to process the application.

faqs.q: Do restaurant and cafe license staff need RSA in Victoria?
faqs.a: The general requirement covers general, on-premises, late night and packaged liquor licenses. Staff at other license types need RSA only if the license carries a special condition requiring it. Venue operators should check the conditions printed on their own license.

faqs.q: What if a staff member has lost their Victorian RSA certificate?
faqs.a: They can get a new certificate free by completing the RSA Refresher course, which needs the certificate number. If they do not have the number, Liquor Control Victoria will verify their details by email and provide it. The refreshed certificate then restarts the three year period.

faqs.q: Is the employer or the employee fined for missing RSA in Victoria?
faqs.a: The offenses in sections 108AA to 108AE of the Liquor Control Reform Act 1998 are framed as licensee obligations: ensuring staff have completed an approved program, keeping certificates on site and producing them on request. Licensees, not individual servers, carry those penalties.

factCheck.claim: Current RSA certificate needed to supply alcohol at general, on-premises, late night and packaged liquor venues where the job includes offering drinks, taking orders or payment for alcohol, or pouring or serving; under 18s can train but cannot serve until 18.
RSA must be completed before starting to supply alcohol or within one month of first supplying it.

Course includes SITHFAB021 plus Victorian topics; a Sexual Harassment and Assault: Recognise, Prevent and Respond module is completed on the LCV Learning Hub before the certificate can be downloaded; refresher is free, about 90 minutes, every 3 years; bridging course requires original training within last 3 years and 10 working days processing.

Licensees must keep a copy of each staff member's current certificate at the venue and make it immediately available to liquor inspectors or Victoria Police; certificate must be no more than 3 years old; Advanced RSA within 6 months of late night licence grant or demerit point.
Offences s108AA(2), s108AA(3), s108AB(2), s108AC(2): maximum $12,546, infringement $1,255; s108AD(2) failure to keep certificates and s108AE(2) failure to produce: maximum $1,046, infringement $105.
